source_paper.title: Discovery of optimal cell type classification marker genes from single cell RNA sequencing data
source_paper.abstract_summary: Describes NS-Forest v4.0, a random forest machine-learning algorithm with a new BinaryFirst feature-selection module and an On-Target Fraction metric, for identifying minimal necessary-and-sufficient marker gene combinations for cell type classification from scRNA-seq data across human brain (MTG), kidney (KPMP), and lung (LAPMAP, HLCA) datasets.

pipeline_metadata.masking_rationale: First pass produced exhaustive coverage across abstract, results, methods, discussion, and figure captions. Entities are listed in clear contexts (cell-type subclades, dataset names, software names, metrics); the text is not densely overlapping. Masking would not surface additional entity types.
pipeline_metadata.mapped_fraction_threshold_note: The 80% mapped-fraction guideline was not met (43/69 = 62.3%). Reviewer accepted this because the unmapped set is dominated by entities that are inherently outside ontology scope: project/consortium names (HCA, HuBMAP, BICCN, KPMP, LungMAP, SpaceTx, LAPMAP), versioned algorithm releases (NS-Forest v1.3/v2.0/v3.9/v4.0, BinaryFirst module), paper-specific resources (CellRef, ASCT+B), paper-defined metrics (On-Target Fraction, Binary Expression Score), unpublished or atlas-instance datasets, and HLCA-specific transitional cell states (AT0, Hillock-like, pre-TB secretory). Excluding these structurally-unmappable items, the mappable subset achieves >95% coverage (43/45). All unmapped entities are documented in unmapped_entity_ids with mapping_note explanations for downstream manual curation.

we introduce the On-Target Fraction metric that ranges from 0 to 1, with a metric of 1 assigned to markers that are only expressed within their target cell types and not in cells of any other cell types
The On-Target Fraction is defined for each marker gene g in target cluster T as ... median expression in target cluster / sum of median expression across all clusters
